beats.trigger: ## From Personal to Team
beats.got: nothing new; it's the module title, and my team is the reason I'm here.

beats.trigger: You can't really share an agent.
beats.got: The thing I wanted to hand my fourteen people can't be handed over as a whole, so I have to choose which part to share.

beats.trigger: Bring one example from your own organisation where people got access to a tool and did not use it.
beats.got: I already have one: the BI licence rollout nobody opened. It's my own company's example, which I prefer.

beats.trigger: **Pick** one of four sharing strategies against the outcome that job needs
beats.got: nothing new; it's a list of verbs, though 'the people plan' caught my eye.

beats.trigger: What would you want a teammate to have: your `memory/` folder, one of your skills, the morning output, or a way to ask the agent a question in Slack?
beats.got: The question is concrete. My gut says the pilot-cohort brief output, but I should say why.

beats.trigger: Start with the teammate's work, not with *"what should I share with my teammate?"*
beats.got: Start from the teammate's job, not from what I built. I've heard Jobs-to-be-Done before from consulting.

beats.trigger: If it could describe anyone in the room, point to the generic line and ask the agent to try that part again.
beats.got: A file naming one teammate, how they do the job today, and an outcome I could observe. I can check that quickly.

beats.trigger: If the reason is *"we already have the platform,"* send it back.
beats.got: Four options with a test for each. 'We have the platform' is exactly the reasoning my team would use, and it isn't a reason.

beats.trigger: [Design the sharing plan](design-the-sharing-plan.md) finds what would stop that candidate from being absorbed
beats.got: nothing new; it's a signpost to the next exercise.

beats.trigger: Find the obstacle that decides whether the teammate can absorb it, then draft both halves of the plan.
beats.got: Next I find the blocker and write two plans, technical and people.

beats.trigger: A good bottleneck explains why several other obstacles stay hard.
beats.got: One blocker should explain several others. That's a useful test, because I'd normally list obstacles flat.

beats.trigger: A polished technical file beside a people file full of unnamed roles is the finding, not a finished rollout.
beats.got: If my people plan has blank owners, it's not ready. That's exactly where my team stalls.

beats.trigger: [Test the sharing plan](test-the-sharing-plan.md) checks the assumptions underneath these plans
beats.got: nothing new; another signpost.

beats.trigger: The technical and people plans are hypotheses.
beats.got: The plans I just wrote are guesses and I should test them.

beats.trigger: *what would have to be true for this teammate, doing this job, to fire their current hire and use my candidate?*
beats.got: Instead of asking how to get adoption, I list what must be true for them to switch, then test two or three of those this week.

beats.trigger: Six months from now, the teammate went back to the incumbent.
beats.got: A pre-mortem that ends in a Monday file: one person, one question, one test. That's usable.

beats.trigger: A candidate picked because it fits the infrastructure is shopping.
beats.got: nothing new; it's a recap of what I just did, and I liked 'shopping' as a word.

beats.trigger: ## Lecture: Access is not absorption
beats.got: nothing new; it's the lecture title.

beats.trigger: The two get reported as one number and they are not one thing.
beats.got: Licences issued and licences used get reported as one adoption number. I recognise that from my own dashboards.

beats.trigger: The proposal got neither a yes nor a no.
beats.got: A solid agent-built analysis died because urgency moved on. I could see my usage-pricing decision going the same way. It was his company, but it fit mine.

beats.trigger: The fourth does not copy at all
beats.got: Context, boundary and checks copy; accountability stays with whoever built it. That's why my agent can't simply become the team's.

beats.trigger: Pick the one your teammate's week can take in.
beats.got: nothing new; this is the four options again, now with what each asks of the receiver.

beats.trigger: Not *how do I get them to adopt this?* but *what would have to be true for them to switch?*
beats.got: nothing new; the exercise made this point already, and here it's said a second time in different words.

beats.trigger: Have the conversation before you build anything more.
beats.got: Talk to one person before I build more. It's sensible and cheap.

beats.trigger: It is rarely the same person across all four.
beats.got: Different teammates need different strategies, and I'll map my fourteen onto them.

beats.trigger: Access is a switch someone flips. Absorption happens in other people's weeks.
beats.got: nothing new; it's a bullet recap of the whole module.

beats.trigger: Their answer is the evidence. The plan is still the hypothesis.
beats.got: I bring what the teammate actually said, not my plan.

beats.got: nothing new; the section is empty.

take_homes: Start from the teammate's job and what they do today, and pick what to share against that outcome. I can't just hand over my agent.
Write the people plan with named owners next to the technical plan, because blank roles are where rollouts die.
Ask what would have to be true for someone to switch, and test two or three of those cheaply before building more.

monday.move: Sit down with the analyst who assembles the pilot-cohort numbers and ask how they build that brief today. Then fill in module-7/monday.md with one assumption and one test.
monday.who: The analyst on the pricing working group who builds the cohort numbers
monday.when: Monday morning, 30 minutes, before I touch any tooling
monday.stop_condition: If their current way of working already gets the brief done and nobody would switch, I stop building and share only the output.
monday.blocker: My team has no shared place for the context files, so even a good result lives in my copy only.

misconception.why: The module is about the teammate's job, the sharing strategy and who owns it, and none of that is prompt wording. It never took the 'better prompts' idea apart directly, so I'm only shaken: my prompts weren't what stalled the BI licences.

one_line: Good for getting from 'I built a thing' to 'one named person, one question, one test'; the lecture repeats the exercises, and I'd cut it by a third.
